Dataset overview

02
DOCUMENTED[S01][S02][S04][S05]
ItemDataset information
DatasetUCSF Renal Mass CT (UCSF RMaC), developed at the University of California San Francisco.
CreatorsSule Sahin and colleagues; project leadership by Peder Larson and Zhen Jane Wang.
PurposeImaging research on renal-mass diagnosis and tumor grade.
Cohort831 CT examinations in the released collection. The paper describes a retrospective search of the 2002–2018 UCSF pathology database for renal masses ≤7 cm. These are examination/case counts; distinct-person linkage is not established here.
AcquisitionsNoncontrast CT and up to three contrast phases. Protocols vary, and some acquisitions came from outside UCSF.
Annotations and labelsSelected renal-mass mask; pathology, tumor type and grade; age, sex and scanner information.
FilesOne HDF5 container per case plus phase_reg_key.csv.
Dataset DOI10.58078/C2WC74
PaperSahin et al., 2026, medRxiv. 10.64898/2026.02.11.26346096
Access and licencePublic AWS dataset; CC BY 4.0, as listed by the AWS Open Data Registry.

The cohort was selected around renal masses and pathology review. Its category frequencies describe this collection, not population disease prevalence.

Root attributes

23 distinct names across the collection: identifiers, clinical labels, scanner/age strings and spacing vectors.

831 rows × 15 columns

What one file holds

Each named CT dataset is a 3D array. The mask is a separate 3D annotation array. Attributes are small values attached to the HDF5 root.

CT phase availability varies by case. The companion CSV adds registration codes and clinical fields, including tumor side, size and procedure type.

Use the exact case ID to join files. Array names such as noncon and CSV columns with the same name represent different kinds of data.

HDF5 inventory depth and storage properties
PropertyObserved information
Array type and storageAll 3,151 inventoried arrays, including masks, are reported as float64 with contiguous storage and no compression.
Dimensions and spacingShapes and *_pixdim vectors vary by case and phase. See Image geometry.
Attributes23 root-attribute names occur across the saved records; individual files contain subsets.
Storage sizeThe tables record logical array bytes, allocated dataset bytes and whole-file size separately.
Inventory scopeThe Python reader inventories root objects and root attributes. The directly inspected example also had no nested groups or extra object attributes.
SOURCE FILES

Master field dictionary

04

Search the arrays, attributes and CSV columns. Select a field to see its meaning, format, values, missing data, sources, and checks to make before use.

Observed presence is case-based. For an attribute, an existing key with a null value is different from an absent key. The field detail panel shows both. Attribute names containing phase suffixes remain separate; their exact naming conventions are UNVERIFIED.

Downloads contain all source entries and the selected analysis fields, with definitions and numerical summaries kept separate.

Image dimensions and voxel spacing

08
CALCULATED

Shape uses stored array axes 0, 1 and 2. Each *_pixdim vector gives their spacing in millimetres. Most arrays have 512 × 512 elements in the first two axes, but 513 × 513 and 496 × 496 arrays also occur.

Line: minimum–maximum. Box: middle 50%. Gold mark: median. The third-axis spacing varies from 0.25 to 10 mm across the CT records.

Stored image values

CALCULATED

All saved CT arrays use float64. The intensity analysis reads every fourth axis-2 slice and the final slice. Percentiles use an additional sample of up to four million finite values per volume.

UNVERIFIED Release-wide Hounsfield Unit calibration is not established by the available files and checks. Values are described here as stored CT values. The sampled ranges are not normalization or clipping recommendations. [S03]
Percentiles and zero values
PhaseMedian p0.1Median p50Median p99.9Median zero %Maximum zero %
noncon-3,024.0-743.0820.00.132%0.286%

These are summaries across per-volume statistics, not pooled voxel percentiles. Whole-image values include background and padding. No NaN or infinity was reported in the sampled slices; unsampled slices were not tested by these statistics.

Percentile samples are converted to float32. Exact zero fractions are shown as percentages so small values do not round to an apparent zero.

SOURCE FILES AND CALCULATED RESULTS

Masks and annotations

10
DOCUMENTED[S01][S03]

The authors used three annotation methods: polygons (about 6%), boxes drawn on slices (53%), and a central box extended using end-slice markers and interpolation (41%). One selected annotation mask was packaged for each annotated exam.

Use the term “annotated-mask volume.” A box includes tissue outside the tumor. Its foreground volume is not a precise measurement of tumor tissue.

CT slice

Stored mask

CT + mask

Actual example: 0MPL7wuVkw, portven, axis-2 index 12. The CT and mask use the same stored shape and spacing; gold marks mask foreground. Display range: −150 to 250 stored values. This illustrates the released annotation, not independently verified tumor boundaries.

Registration and its recorded status

11
DOCUMENTED[S01][S03]

The noncontrast image is the fixed reference. The authors cropped the contrast volumes and masks along the slice axis, then used ANTs affine registration with Mattes mutual information. Deformable registration was tried; affine was selected. Failed ANTs cases were also attempted with DIPY affine registration.

SELECTED ANALYSIS RESULTS

Data checks

16

These checks identify specific records worth examining before an analysis. A flagged record is not automatically corrupt, and the findings do not imply a single exclusion rule.

CALCULATED
CheckFindingPractical meaning
Case files and IDs831 reported readable; no saved case errors. No duplicate CSV IDs or unmatched case-ID sets.The supplied records join successfully. “Readable” by itself means the container opened.
Phase presence: CSV versus saved HDF5 inventoryCONFLICTING 4 phase entries across 2 casesCSV code 1 says the volume exists, but the saved inventory has no corresponding key. Confirm these raw files before selecting cases by CSV alone.
Shape of code-2 volumes5 shape-mismatch entries across 4 cases: 3 masks and 2 portven volumesReview the raw geometry before treating every code-2 volume as sharing the noncon grid.
Other shape differences535 of 540 mismatch rows carry code 1Most shape differences occur in volumes explicitly marked unregistered.
Mask continuity13 masks have two components; 10 have slice gapsInspect if the task depends on connected regions or contiguous annotation. These are separate checks and may overlap.
Large zero fraction29 CT volumes in 22 cases have >50% zeros in the sampled slicesInspect the displayed field of view and foreground before choosing normalization or cropping.
Image-value range flag50 CT volumes in 28 cases fail the software’s HU-like range heuristicA numerical review flag, not proof that a file is corrupt or that the remaining values are calibrated HU.
Extra root attributes41 cases have additional Manufacturer or Patient Age attribute namesRetain the recorded metadata. An unexpected name is not inherently invalid.

Research use

19

The broader Kidney-VLM project includes image analysis, segmentation, image measurements and a vision-language component. RMaC can supply some of those inputs; the table below describes the available evidence without selecting an individual research hypothesis.

Research needWhat is available in the inspected RMaC filesWhat this supports or still requires
Multiphase image analysisCT arrays, phase names, spacing and registration codesCase selection and phase-specific inputs; missing phases and alignment need explicit handling.
Renal-mass localizationOne binary mask for an annotated case; mostly box-based annotation methodsRegion selection and annotation-based supervision. Precise tumor-boundary evaluation needs an appropriate reference.
Diagnosis and grade targetsPathology phrases, broad tumor categories, grade codesLabel-defined cohorts; retain uncertain phrases and state grouping rules. These labels must not leak into prediction inputs.
Image measurementsStored spacing, images, annotation extent and a CSV size fieldAnnotation measurements are possible; validated tumor volume, necrosis and rim-enhancement measurements need suitable region definitions and image units.
Dataset variationAge, sex, scanner/system strings, phase availability and geometryDescriptive subgroup and acquisition analysis. These variables do not establish causal effects.
Language supervisionShort diagnostic labels and structured clinical fieldsNo full radiology report, full pathology report or ready-made question–answer field was found in the inspected schema. Generated text would be a new derived resource.
Other imaging and clinical outcomesNo MRI, ultrasound, pathology slide array, kidney/stone mask, longitudinal outcome or survival field in the inspected schemaThose inputs or targets would need another documented source.
Data splittingAnonymized case IDsUse IDs for joins and split tracking. A verified cross-exam patient link and duplicate-content assessment are not supplied here.

Medical & technical glossary

20

CT

Computed tomography reconstructs cross-sectional images from X-ray measurements. A volume contains many slices; a multiphase exam contains several acquisitions.

[M07]

Contrast agent

An administered substance that changes image appearance. Intravenous iodinated contrast helps reveal blood vessels, perfusion and urinary excretion in CT.

[M07]

Attenuation

Reduction of X-ray beam intensity as it passes through tissue. CT reconstruction estimates spatial differences related to this physical interaction.

[M11]

Hounsfield Unit (HU)

A calibrated CT attenuation scale referenced to water (0) and approximately air (−1000). An HU-like range is not proof that a released array preserves calibrated HU.

[M11][M10]

Renal mass

A localized abnormality in or associated with the kidney. A mass is not automatically cancer; pathology may identify benign, malignant or non-neoplastic causes.

[M01][S01]

RCC

Renal cell carcinoma: a family of malignant kidney epithelial tumors with several histologic subtypes. It is not a synonym for every renal mass.

[M01]

Clear-cell RCC

A renal cancer subtype named for its microscopic cellular appearance. The label describes pathology, not simply the brightness of a CT image.

[M03]

Papillary RCC

A distinct renal cell carcinoma histology. Preserve historical subtype wording rather than automatically translating it into a newer classification.

[M04]

Chromophobe RCC

A distinct renal cell carcinoma histology, biologically different from clear-cell RCC. A generic oncocytic phrase does not uniquely identify it.

[M05]

Oncocytoma

A conventional benign renal tumor. A mixed or uncertain oncocytic diagnosis should not automatically be normalized to oncocytoma.

[M09]

Angiomyolipoma (AML)

A usually benign renal tumor with fatty, muscular and vascular components. The broad AML category should not erase unusual or uncertain diagnostic wording.

[M06]

Pathology

Examination and interpretation of disease in tissue or cells. In this dictionary, pathology is the stored diagnostic phrase supplied with an exam.

[M01][S01]

Histology

Microscopic tissue structure and the disease classification based on it. Histology labels and tumor grade describe different aspects of a diagnosis.

[M02][M03]

Grade

A pathology assessment of cellular features associated with tumor behavior. Grade differs from stage; grading systems vary. RMaC codes5/6 are unspecified high/low bands.

[M02][S01]

Stage

An assessment of anatomical extent, such as size and spread. The paper describes ≤7cm/T1 inclusion; do not infer detailed stage from annotation volume.

[M01][S01]

Biopsy

Acquisition of tissue for pathological examination. The RMaC procedure column also includes nephrectomies, so its name is broader than needle biopsy alone.

[M01][S01]

Nephrectomy

Surgical removal of kidney tissue: partial removes part of the kidney; radical removes the kidney with additional surrounding structures as indicated.

[M01]

Corticomedullary phase

Early post-contrast renal imaging emphasizing differences between cortex and medulla. RMaC groups relevant timing under arterial.

[S01]

Nephrographic phase

Post-contrast renal imaging with more uniform parenchymal enhancement. RMaC includes relevant timing under its broader portven category.

[S01]

Portal venous phase

A contrast timing category commonly used for abdominal imaging. RMaC portven includes scans labeled nephrographic; timing is not standardized per case.

[S01]

Delayed / excretory phase

Later imaging after contrast injection, often showing contrast excretion into the collecting system. RMaC groups these under delay.

[S01][M07]

Segmentation

An assignment of labels to pixels or voxels. A filled bounding box is a spatial annotation but is not a precise tissue-boundary segmentation.

[S01]

Enhancement

An image-value change related to contrast administration. Interpretation requires comparable anatomy, acquisition context and a justified intensity scale.

[S01][M07]

Diagnosis versus prognosis

Diagnosis identifies the disease; prognosis concerns its expected future course. RMaC diagnosis/grade labels do not constitute longitudinal outcome data.

[M03][M02]

Benign versus malignant

Benign indicates noncancerous; malignant indicates cancer. This distinction cannot be inferred safely from the numeric order of RMaC tumor_type codes.

[M01][M06]

HDF5

A hierarchical container format that stores named objects and associated attributes. One RMaC case is packaged in one HDF5 file.

[S09a][S01]

Case / exam

A release record corresponding to a packaged exam. Do not assume arbitrary filename changes preserve patient identity or that patient overlap across releases is resolved.

[S01][S02]

Dataset (HDF5 object)

A named array inside an HDF5 container, such as /noncon. Distinct from the word dataset meaning the whole RMaC collection.

[S09b]

Group

An HDF5 container for named child objects, similar to a directory. Every file has a root group.

[S09a]

Attribute

A named metadata value attached to an HDF5 object. RMaC clinical/spacing attributes in the supplied inventory are on the root group.

[S09a]

Metadata

Information describing data, such as spacing, scanner system, diagnosis label or identifier. It can be native, derived or inferred; those origins differ.

[S01]

Array

An indexed collection of numbers. Here a 3D array uses three indices; index order alone does not determine anatomical orientation.

[S09b]

Shape

Number of elements along each array axis, for example512×512×35. Equal shapes do not guarantee corresponding anatomy.

[S09b]

dtype

The numerical/storage type of an element, such as float64. A type describes representation, not the physical unit.

[S09b]

Pixel

An element of a two-dimensional image plane. Physical pixel size must come from valid geometric metadata.

[S10]

Voxel

An element of a three-dimensional image grid. Its nominal physical volume is the product of three valid grid-spacing components.

[S10]

Pixel / voxel spacing

Distance between neighboring grid locations along array axes. Stored spacing does not include the complete orientation or origin.

[S10][S01]

Slice thickness

Nominal reconstructed slice thickness, a distinct acquisition/reconstruction concept from spacing between slice centers. Legacy RMaC audit naming conflates these.

[S10]

Anisotropy

Unequal sampling resolution along different axes. A thin in-plane grid with larger between-plane spacing is anisotropic.

[S10]

Field of view

The physical region covered by an acquisition or reconstructed grid. Nominal array extent can be estimated as n×spacing, with the chosen convention stated.

[S01][S10]

Registration

Estimating a spatial transform that aligns a moving image with a fixed reference. Status labels are different from independent measurements of alignment accuracy.

[M08][S01]

Fixed versus moving image

The fixed image supplies the reference coordinate grid; the moving image is transformed to align with it. RMaC uses noncon as reference.

[S01][M08]

Affine transformation

A spatial mapping allowing translation, rotation, scale and shear. It cannot represent arbitrary local tissue deformation.

[M08]

Deformable registration

Registration with spatially varying transformations that can model local deformation. The RMaC paper reports attempts but describes affine transforms for the selected workflow.

[S01]

Mutual information

A statistical dependence measure used as an image-alignment objective. It can support registration when corresponding tissues have different intensity patterns.

[M08]

Resampling

Evaluating an image on a new grid using interpolation. It can create fractional intensities; integer-range bounds alone do not make int16 conversion lossless.

[M08]

Mask

An array of labels marking regions. In RMaC, foreground denotes the selected annotation extent, often derived from boxes.

[S01]

Bounding box

An axis-aligned rectangular region in2D or cuboid in3D. It can contain background and other tissue around the target.

[S01]

Connected component

A set of foreground voxels linked under a specified neighbor rule. Components need not correspond one-to-one to lesions.

Chunking

Partitioning an HDF5 dataset into blocks for storage/access. Access efficiency depends on layout and the shape of read requests.

[S09b]

Table grain

The entity represented by one row, such as a case, case×phase or anomaly. Denominators and joins must respect it.

Exact / sampled / approximate / derived

Exact counts use all values in the declared scope; sampled quantities inspect a subset; approximate methods alter numerical representation/estimation; derived values are calculated. These labels can overlap.

ML leakage

Use of information unavailable at the intended prediction time, or exposure of the answer through inputs or splits. Diagnosis and grade labels are obvious risks for corresponding prediction tasks.
